slides.headline: OpenAI's AI solved the math problem nobody cracked in 90 years
slides.body: 10,000 AI agents ran in parallel and cracked the Navier-Stokes equations in just 88 hours. This is one of math's 7 Millennium Prize Problems with a $1 million bounty that has sat unclaimed for roughly 90 years

slides.headline: A mathematician says OpenAI built its breakthrough on his stolen work
slides.body: Tristan Buckmaster spent a year working on Navier-Stokes with AI. He says his work leaked to OpenAI, who raced ahead, then pressured him to remove his co-author from the paper because that person works at Anthropic

slides.headline: Google built an AI database mapping 9 billion DNA mutations
slides.body: AlphaGenome Atlas predicts the impact of every possible single-letter change to human DNA, covering all 9 billion variations. Researchers can now look up any mutation and get its predicted effect on biology, without running a single lab test

slides.headline: Students not using AI chatbots are getting better grades
slides.body: A Bloomberg study found students who avoid AI chatbots for schoolwork are consistently scoring higher than those who use them. It's the opposite of what most people assumed, and it raises a sharp question about whether AI helps students learn or just helps them skip the thinking

slides.headline: The top AI labs are swapping the crown faster than ever
slides.body: Analysts had OpenAI pegged as falling behind in the AI race just weeks ago. The leapfrog between the top labs is now so fast that last month's laggard can become this month's leader before a benchmark even gets published

slides.headline: SAVE TODAY'S AI BRIEFING
slides.body:
• OpenAI's AI cracked Navier-Stokes, a 90-year $1M math problem, in 88 hours
• The mathematician who got there first says OpenAI used his stolen research
• Google's AlphaGenome Atlas maps all 9 billion possible DNA mutations
• Bloomberg: students avoiding AI chatbots score higher grades
• The AI leapfrog between top labs is faster than any benchmark can track
